scorecard.methodology: Brier/log score over resolved YES/NO published forecast windows; VOID and pending entries are counted for coverage but excluded from accuracy math. The ledger totals and the maturity funnel count published forecasts only: shadow bets, scored for evidence but never shown, are left out of them. Each window is one question, and it is scored on the probability published when the window opened; a later re-emission of the same question does not change it. While an outcome-fitted calibration gate passes, that probability is calibrated, and the API does not mark which ones are; after a switch between raw and calibrated publication, the rolling window mixes forecasts published under both. 120 forecasts scored against a data feed we could not read correctly are voided and left out of every score (issue #5233). 322 shadow bet windows that opened on a base-rate placeholder instead of a model forecast are left out of every count, VOID included (issue #8990). Since 8 October 2026, 2 of 3 resolved published forecasts were void (66.7%, 95% interval 20.8% to 93.9%). That is too few to compare with the target of under 15%, which needs at least 30 resolved. Judged forecasts resolve days after hard ones and have voided more often, so early readings run low. This counts published forecasts first issued on or after that date, so it leaves out unpublished shadow bets and the voids relabelled in the issue #8990 audit.
